title: Proof of frobenius s classification
html:
Proof. Proof of frobenius s classification

Proof. We verify each S-eigenvalue in turn.

Coefficients. The action q \mapsto q^{-1} extends to the underlying field of fractions and acts on each coefficient:

  • D = q^4 + 4q^2 + 1 is palindromic in q^2: under q \to q^{-1}, D \to q^{-4} + 4q^{-2} + 1 = q^{-4}(1 + 4q^2 + q^4) = q^{-4} D. Then W_{\mathrm{sym}} = q^2/D \to q^{-2}/(q^{-4} D) = q^2/D, invariant. Same for W_{\mathrm{alt}}. For W_{\mathrm{std}}: (q^2+1)^2 \to (q^{-2}+1)^2 = q^{-4}(1+q^2)^2, so W_{\mathrm{std}} \to q^{-4}(1+q^2)^2 / (q^{-4} D) = W_{\mathrm{std}}.
  • [3]_q = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}: invariant under q \to q^{-1}.
  • h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} \to q^{-1} - q = -h_{\mathrm{A}}, so h_{\mathrm{A}} has eigenvalue -1 and h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 has eigenvalue +1.
  • z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}): the denominator is symmetric under q \to q^{-1}, so z is invariant.
  • Catalan's constant G, Borromean volume 8G, electron mass m_e, and binding scale \alpha are real canonical constants unaffected by the algebraic action.

Functional \Phi_2. The transfer matrix is T(c, d) = \begin{pmatrix} ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d & c \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} with \det T = d(ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d) - c^2. The Frobenius antipode maps the primitive factor (c, d) to (c, d - ch_{\mathrm{A}}) (this swaps \sigma \leftrightarrow \sigma^{-1}). Direct computation:

See Table 3.

For each primitive the determinant is S-invariant. Since \det is multiplicative on chain products, \Phi_2 = \sum_i \log\lvert\det M_i\rvert is S-invariant.

Functional \Phi_3. For each primitive, direct computation shows \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(S(c, d)) = -\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(c, d) and \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(S(c, d)) = -\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(c, d) (verify: for (1, 0) with \chi^{\mathrm{sym}} = q, \chi^{\mathrm{alt}} = -1/q, and S(1, 0) = (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}) giving \chi^{\mathrm{sym}} = q + (-h_{\mathrm{A}}) = q^{-1} and \chi^{\mathrm{alt}} = -1/q + (-h_{\mathrm{A}}) = -q, matching the swap with sign). For a chain product

  \frac{\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(S(\beta))}{\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(S(\beta))}
  = \frac{(-1)^n \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(\beta)}{(-1)^n \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(\beta)}
  = \left(\frac{\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(\beta)}{\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(\beta)}\right)^{-1}

so \Phi_3(S(\beta)) = -\Phi_3(\beta), eigenvalue -1.

Functional \Phi_1. The unsymmetrised standard character \chi^{\mathrm{std}}(\beta) is not an S-eigenvector in general. The Frobenius-symmetrised value V_{\mathrm{Frob}} = (\chi^{\mathrm{std}}(\beta) + \chi^{\mathrm{std}}(S(\beta)))/2 is by construction S-invariant. Equivalently, the average \Phi_1 := \tfrac12 (\Phi_1(\beta) + \Phi_1(S(\beta))) is the projection onto the S-even subspace. \square

Corollary. The signed sum

  \mathfrak{m}(S(\beta)) - \mathfrak{m}(\beta)
  = -2 \alpha h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3(\beta)

isolates the chirality channel as the unique source of S-odd contribution to the categorical mass. canonical, since S maps the proton braid (uud) to a braid with quark content (ddu) (modulo strand ordering equivalent to the neutron's udd content), this provides the structural origin of the proton-neutron mass splitting at the Wedderburn formula level.

Witness: the formal derivation verifies the eigenvalue assignments canonical at q_0 and confirms that \Phi_3 \approx 0 for inter-nucleon-only chains in free A=1 nucleons (consistent with the S-eigenspace decomposition).
